note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English; the original uses the old combination Eutermes carnarvonensis (now placed in Nasutitermes). In the alate measurements the pronotum length and width and the fore wing width, in the soldier the head width, and in the worker the head length to the clypeofrontal suture are broken and damaged in the OCR; this is stated as it stands rather than filled in with figures.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) was published under the name Eutermes carnarvonensis, with the type locality at Carnarvon Range, Queensland. The alate, which is larger and brown with long brown wings with a yellow costal margin, can be distinguished from E. exitiosus; the soldier, however, has no reliable character distinguishing it from the soldier of E. exitiosus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A larger brown species with long brown wings with a yellow costal margin. Head dark chestnut brown; postclypeus, pronotum, wing pads and lateral margins of the abdominal tergites slightly paler; median abdominal tergites yellow brown, anterior halves of mesothorax and metathorax and legs paler; abdominal tergites pale yellow brown. Head, thorax and abdomen only moderately hairy. Compound eyes large, with a transparent rim. Ocelli rather small. Fontanelle distinct. Postclypeus slightly less than half as long as wide (original Fig. 186). Second mandibular tooth about as long as the first but slightly wider. Antennae 15-segmented; segments 2 and 5 about equal and the shortest of the whole antenna, or segment 5 slightly shorter than segment 2; segment 3 only slightly longer than segment 4, about as long as segment 6. Media usually with 6 or 7 short oblique radial branches. Measurements: length with wings 19.50—20.00; length without wings 8.00—9.00; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.76—1.83; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.02—1.17; head width 1.57—1.61; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.58—0.60; ocellus length 0.15—0.17; fore wing length 15.50; the figures for pronotum length, pronotum width and fore wing width are damaged in the OCR and could not be read.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The original states that the soldier of this species has no reliable character distinguishing it from the soldier of E. exitiosus (Figs. 187—188). Measurements: total length 4.10—4.20; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.87—1.90; pronotum width 0.58; the figure for head width is given in the OCR as "lho ! 1.'17°", damaged and illegible.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head mostly pale chestnut brown, with two fairly distinct longitudinal lines on each side of the vertex, the innermost pair the shortest and least distinct; postclypeus pale yellow brown. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 4 the shortest. Postclypeus about half as long as wide. Measurements: total length 5.00—5.50; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.78—1.83; head width 1.57; pronotum width 0.84—0.88; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) given in the OCR as "i°o§ 1,10", damaged and illegible.
